title: World Bank adds $95m to urban services project for municipalities
excerpt: Bangladesh and the World Bank signed $95 million in extra financing for the Resilient Urban and Territorial Development Project on 15 November.
content:
Bangladesh and the World Bank signed an additional $95 million for the Resilient Urban and Territorial Development Project (RUTDP) on 15 November, The Business Standard reported. The money replaces $95 million moved earlier from the project's original $400 million to its emergency response component.

Of the total, $92 million comes from IDA's Scale-up Window Shorter Maturity Loan, with no interest, service charge or commitment fee and a 12-year term including six years' grace. The other $3 million carries 1.5% interest over 25 years, with five years' grace.

The project aims to improve basic urban services, strengthen municipal governance and financial management, and raise local revenue. It also builds planning, procurement and financial management skills in pourashavas and city corporations. The financing is meant to help finish the project by June 2030. ERD Secretary Md Shahriar Kader Siddiky and Jean Pesme, World Bank Division Director for Bangladesh and Bhutan, signed the deal.

Why it matters

Municipal services such as drainage, roads and waste collection shape health and flood risk in fast-growing towns. NGOs working on urban poverty, WASH and local governance may find openings to work with participating municipalities on planning and accountability.
